title: Preterite versus imperfect
objectives: I can choose between the preterite and the imperfect depending on whether I am narrating an event or describing the background.
I can tell a story with a setting, a sudden event and a result.
I can explain what was happening when something else occurred, using estava plus a gerund with quando and enquanto.
I can use saber, conhecer, querer, poder and ter with the correct meaning in each past tense.
I can give excuses and explanations with porque, por causa de and felizmente.

example.pt: De repente, a luz apagou.
example.en: Suddenly, the light went out.

example.pt: Enquanto eu cozinhava, meu filho fazia a lição de casa.
example.en: While I cooked, my son did his homework.

example.pt: Naquele dia, chovia muito e o trânsito estava parado.
example.en: That day, it was raining hard and traffic was at a standstill.

example.pt: Na hora, eu não entendi nada.
example.en: At the moment, I did not understand anything.

example.pt: Vi um acidente na avenida ontem.
example.en: I saw an accident on the avenue yesterday.

vocabulary.en: to hit, to crash, to knock

example.pt: Ele bateu o carro num poste.
example.en: He crashed the car into a pole.

vocabulary.note: Preterite: caí, caiu, caímos, caíram. Imperfect: caía. The accent marks the separate vowel sound.

example.pt: Eu caí da bicicleta, mas não me machuquei.
example.en: I fell off the bicycle, but I did not get hurt.

vocabulary.note: The eu form of the preterite is escorreguei.

example.pt: Ela escorregou no chão molhado.
example.en: She slipped on the wet floor.

example.pt: Caí e quebrei o braço.
example.en: I fell and broke my arm.

vocabulary.note: Usually reflexive for yourself: me machuquei, se machucou.

example.pt: Ele se machucou jogando futebol.
example.en: He hurt himself playing soccer.

vocabulary.en: to puncture, to get a flat tire

example.pt: O pneu furou no meio da estrada.
example.en: The tire went flat in the middle of the road.

example.pt: Faltou luz no bairro inteiro.
example.en: The power went out in the whole neighborhood.

vocabulary.note: Levar um susto means to get a scare.

example.pt: Levei um susto quando o telefone tocou.
example.en: I got a scare when the phone rang.

example.pt: O barulho assustou todo mundo.
example.en: The noise startled everybody.

example.pt: Ouvi um barulho forte na cozinha.
example.en: I heard a loud noise in the kitchen.

example.pt: A festa foi uma surpresa boa.
example.en: The party was a nice surprise.

vocabulary.note: Singular: uma notícia. The plural as notícias means the news in general.

example.pt: Li a notícia no jornal hoje de manhã.
example.en: I read the news in the newspaper this morning.

example.pt: Cheguei atrasado por causa do trânsito.
example.en: I arrived late because of the traffic.

vocabulary.note: Often reflexive: me atrasei. With cheguei atrasado, the adjective agrees in gender.

example.pt: Atrasei porque perdi o ônibus.
example.en: I was late because I missed the bus.

vocabulary.note: Pedir desculpa means to apologize. Desculpa! is the everyday way to say sorry.

example.pt: Pedi desculpa pelo atraso.
example.en: I apologized for the delay.

example.pt: Por causa da chuva, a gente não saiu.
example.en: Because of the rain, we did not go out.

example.pt: Derrubei o copo sem querer.
example.en: I knocked over the glass by accident.

example.pt: Felizmente, ninguém se machucou.
example.en: Luckily, nobody got hurt.

example.pt: Infelizmente, eu não pude ir à festa.
example.en: Unfortunately, I could not go to the party.

vocabulary.note: Common patterns: ter medo de, ficar com medo, sentir medo.

example.pt: Na hora, senti muito medo.
example.en: At that moment, I felt very afraid.

example.pt: Eu estava nervoso porque a prova era difícil.
example.en: I was nervous because the test was difficult.

example.pt: Fiquei aliviado quando ele ligou.
example.en: I was relieved when he called.

example.pt: Minha mãe estava preocupada porque eu não atendia o telefone.
example.en: My mother was worried because I did not answer the phone.

example.pt: Percebi que estava sem a carteira.
example.en: I realized that I did not have my wallet.

example.pt: Descobri a verdade ontem.
example.en: I found out the truth yesterday.

example.pt: Alguém chamou a ambulância.
example.en: Someone called the ambulance.

dialogues.title: Why were you late?
dialogues.context: Diego arrives late to work and explains to his manager, Sandra, what happened.

lines.speaker: Sandra
lines.pt: Diego, você chegou às dez. O que aconteceu?
lines.en: Diego, you arrived at ten. What happened?

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.pt: Desculpa, Sandra. Eu saí de casa às sete, mas o pneu furou no meio da avenida.
lines.en: Sorry, Sandra. I left home at seven, but the tire went flat in the middle of the avenue.

lines.speaker: Sandra
lines.pt: Que chato! E você chamou alguém?
lines.en: How annoying! And did you call someone?

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.pt: Chamei o seguro, mas o atendimento demorou. Enquanto eu esperava, começou a chover.
lines.en: I called the insurance, but the service took a long time. While I was waiting, it started to rain.

lines.speaker: Sandra
lines.pt: Nossa. E você não tinha o celular?
lines.en: Wow. And did you not have your phone?

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.pt: Tinha, mas a bateria acabou. Por isso eu não avisei. Já pedi desculpa pro cliente também.
lines.en: I did, but the battery died. That is why I did not let you know. I already apologized to the client too.

lines.speaker: Sandra
lines.pt: Tudo bem. Felizmente a reunião só começou às dez e meia.
lines.en: That is fine. Luckily the meeting only started at ten thirty.

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.pt: Que alívio! Amanhã eu saio mais cedo, prometo.
lines.en: What a relief! Tomorrow I will leave earlier, I promise.

dialogues.title: You will not believe what happened
dialogues.context: Marina tells her friends Felipe and Carol about a scare on her bicycle.

lines.speaker: Marina
lines.pt: Gente, vocês não vão acreditar no que aconteceu ontem.
lines.en: Guys, you will not believe what happened yesterday.

lines.speaker: Felipe
lines.pt: O que foi? Conta!
lines.en: What was it? Tell us!

lines.speaker: Marina
lines.pt: Eu estava andando de bicicleta no parque, ouvindo música, quando de repente um cachorro atravessou na minha frente.
lines.en: I was riding my bike in the park, listening to music, when suddenly a dog ran across in front of me.

lines.speaker: Carol
lines.pt: Meu Deus! E aí?
lines.en: Oh my God! And then?

lines.speaker: Marina
lines.pt: Eu freei, escorreguei e caí. Levei um susto enorme.
lines.en: I braked, slipped and fell. I got a huge scare.

lines.speaker: Felipe
lines.pt: Você se machucou?
lines.en: Did you get hurt?

lines.speaker: Marina
lines.pt: Felizmente não. Só machuquei o joelho.
lines.en: Luckily not. I only hurt my knee.

lines.speaker: Carol
lines.pt: E o cachorro?
lines.en: And the dog?

lines.speaker: Marina
lines.pt: Saiu correndo. O dono veio pedir desculpa e ainda me pagou um sorvete!
lines.en: It ran off. The owner came to apologize and even bought me an ice cream!

lines.speaker: Felipe
lines.pt: Que história! Eu estava em casa dormindo e nem fiquei sabendo.
lines.en: What a story! I was at home sleeping and did not even hear about it.

dialogues.title: Did you know her?
dialogues.context: At a party, Helena and Bruno talk about Patrícia, the new boss, and what each of them knew.

lines.speaker: Helena
lines.pt: Bruno, você conhece a Patrícia?
lines.en: Bruno, do you know Patrícia?

lines.speaker: Bruno
lines.pt: Conheço. Eu conheci a Patrícia na faculdade. Eu sabia que ela trabalhava aqui, mas só soube hoje que ela é a nova chefe.
lines.en: I do. I met Patrícia in college. I knew she worked here, but I only found out today that she is the new boss.

lines.speaker: Helena
lines.pt: Eu também só soube hoje! Quando eu encontrei a Patrícia, eu queria falar com ela, mas ela estava ocupada.
lines.en: I only found out today too! When I ran into Patrícia, I wanted to talk to her, but she was busy.

lines.speaker: Bruno
lines.pt: E depois? Você tentou de novo?
lines.en: And then? Did you try again?

lines.speaker: Helena
lines.pt: Tentei, mas não pude. Ela saiu correndo pra uma reunião.
lines.en: I did, but I could not. She rushed off to a meeting.

lines.speaker: Bruno
lines.pt: Então vamos falar com ela agora. Ela está ali, com o pessoal do financeiro.
lines.en: Then let us talk to her now. She is over there with the finance team.

lines.speaker: Helena
lines.pt: Boa ideia. Quem sabe ela ainda se lembra de você.
lines.en: Good idea. Maybe she still remembers you.

grammar.title: Event or background?
grammar.explanation:
The core question is simple. Use the preterite for events that moved the story forward: things that happened, were finished, or happened a specific number of times. Use the imperfect for the stage the events happened on: weather, time, age, feelings, habits, and actions that were in progress. The preterite answers 'What happened?' and the imperfect answers 'What was it like?' or 'What was going on?'

Compare: Ontem choveu means it rained (as an event, starting and ending). Chovia quando eu saí means it was raining when I left (the scene). Both are correct, but they tell different stories. The words you use can help you choose: time markers such as ontem, de repente, uma vez and naquele dia point to the preterite, while antigamente, sempre, todo dia and enquanto point to the imperfect.

Another way to decide is to imagine a film. The imperfect is the camera panning over the scene, and the preterite is each action in the plot. A single sentence can contain both: Eu estava cansado (scene), então dormi cedo (event).

examples.pt: Ontem choveu o dia todo.
examples.en: Yesterday it rained all day.

examples.pt: Quando eu saí, chovia muito.
examples.en: When I left, it was raining hard.

examples.pt: Eu estava cansado, então dormi cedo.
examples.en: I was tired, so I went to sleep early.

examples.pt: Todo dia eu caminhava, mas naquele dia eu fiquei em casa.
examples.en: Every day I walked, but that day I stayed home.

examples.pt: Eles eram jovens quando se casaram.
examples.en: They were young when they got married.

grammar.title: An action interrupted: estava plus gerund and quando
grammar.explanation:
The classic pattern for a story has a long action in progress and a short event that interrupts it. The ongoing action goes in the imperfect, often the progressive (estava plus a gerund), and the interrupting event goes in the preterite: Eu estava dormindo quando o telefone tocou. The connecting word is normally quando, and the order can be reversed: O telefone tocou quando eu estava dormindo.

For two actions happening at the same time, both verbs go in the imperfect and the connector is enquanto: Enquanto eu cozinhava, ele estudava. For a sudden event, de repente is the most natural signal and is followed by the preterite: De repente, a luz apagou.

In speech, people also use the plain imperfect instead of the progressive. Eu dormia quando o telefone tocou is correct and sounds slightly more literary. In Brazil, the progressive is very natural and expected in oral storytelling. Finally, when two short events happen one after another, both verbs are in the preterite: Quando o telefone tocou, eu acordei.

examples.pt: Eu estava andando quando começou a chover.
examples.en: I was walking when it started to rain.

examples.pt: Enquanto eu cozinhava, meu filho fazia a lição.
examples.en: While I was cooking, my son was doing his homework.

examples.pt: De repente, a porta abriu e todo mundo gritou surpresa.
examples.en: Suddenly, the door opened and everybody shouted surprise.

examples.pt: A gente conversava quando a luz apagou.
examples.en: We were chatting when the power went out.

examples.pt: Quando o telefone tocou, eu acordei.
examples.en: When the phone rang, I woke up.

grammar.title: Verbs that change meaning: saber, conhecer, querer, poder, ter
grammar.explanation:
Some verbs express a state in the imperfect and a change or event in the preterite, and their English translation changes. Saber in the imperfect means 'knew' (sabia), but in the preterite it means 'found out' (soube). Conhecer in the imperfect means 'knew (someone)', while conheci means 'met for the first time'.

Querer gives queria (wanted) versus quis (tried to, decided to); the negative não quis means 'refused'. Poder gives podia (was able to, could) versus pude (managed to, succeeded), while não pude means 'could not and did not'. With ter que, tinha que means 'had to' (without saying if it happened) and tive que means 'had to and did'. Finally, ter in the preterite can also mean 'got' or 'received': Tive notícias boas.

These pairs are worth memorizing as blocks. The imperfect describes a state of mind or ability, and the preterite reports the result at a specific moment.

rows: conheci: met for the first time
pude: managed to; não pude: could not

examples.pt: Eu sabia a resposta, mas só soube da notícia hoje.
examples.en: I knew the answer, but only found out about the news today.

examples.pt: Eu conhecia o Pedro, mas conheci a irmã dele ontem.
examples.en: I knew Pedro, but I met his sister yesterday.

examples.pt: Eu queria sair, mas ele não quis.
examples.en: I wanted to go out, but he refused.

examples.pt: Eu queria ajudar, mas não pude porque estava doente.
examples.en: I wanted to help, but I was not able to because I was sick.

examples.pt: Ontem tive que trabalhar até tarde.
examples.en: Yesterday I had to work until late.

grammar.title: Building a story and giving explanations
grammar.explanation:
A clear story has three parts. First the setting, in the imperfect: Era sábado, chovia e eu estava em casa. Then the trigger, in the preterite with de repente or quando: De repente, ouvi um barulho. Finally the result, in the preterite: Levei um susto, mas felizmente não aconteceu nada. Adding feelings in the past also uses the imperfect: Eu estava nervoso, Ela estava preocupada.

To give an explanation, the natural pattern is a preterite result plus porque and a reason: Atrasei porque perdi o ônibus, or with the imperfect for a continuing cause: Não atendi porque estava dormindo. Por causa de is followed by a noun: Por causa do trânsito, cheguei atrasado.

Remember that porque (one word, without accent) answers a question, while por que (two words) asks it: Por que você se atrasou? In Brazilian speech, it is natural to say Desculpa! at the beginning of an explanation, and Pedi desculpa pelo atraso when you report it later.

examples.pt: Era sábado e chovia. De repente, faltou luz.
examples.en: It was Saturday and it was raining. Suddenly, the power went out.

examples.pt: Atrasei porque perdi o ônibus.
examples.en: I was late because I missed the bus.

examples.pt: Não atendi porque estava dormindo.
examples.en: I did not answer because I was sleeping.

examples.pt: Por causa do trânsito, cheguei atrasado.
examples.en: Because of the traffic, I arrived late.

examples.pt: Por que você não avisou?
examples.en: Why did you not let me know?

culture.title: Trânsito, desculpas and good stories
culture.text:
In big Brazilian cities, the most common excuse for being late is o trânsito. In São Paulo or Rio de Janeiro, people really do spend hours commuting, so colleagues usually accept it. Saying Desculpa o atraso, o trânsito estava um caos is normal and polite. Punctuality is generally more flexible than in some other countries, especially for social events, but for work meetings and appointments it is still important to warn people, often with a quick WhatsApp message like Estou chegando, cinco minutinhos.

Brazilians love to tell stories, and the way they tell them is lively. People use many reactions: Nossa!, Meu Deus!, Que susto!, Ainda bem!, Ufa! and Graças a Deus. Short voice messages on WhatsApp, called áudios, are often used to tell a full story in a minute or two, and the listener answers with laughing or surprised reactions. A good story includes details of the scene and a sudden turn, which is exactly the structure of imperfect and preterite.

News reports follow a similar style. On television and in newspapers, a short report normally starts with the facts in the preterite, Um ciclista caiu na tarde de ontem, and then gives the context in the imperfect, Ele andava pela ciclovia quando um cachorro atravessou. Learning to read these texts is an excellent way to practice the contrast between the two tenses.

paragraphs.pt: Naquele dia, chovia muito e o trânsito estava parado. Eu estava em casa, cozinhando, enquanto meu filho fazia a lição de casa na sala.
paragraphs.en: That day, it was raining hard and traffic was at a standstill. I was at home, cooking, while my son did his homework in the living room.

paragraphs.pt: De repente, a luz apagou e ouvimos um barulho forte lá fora. Meu filho levou um susto enorme. Eu acendi uma vela e expliquei que era só uma árvore que caiu na rua.
paragraphs.en: Suddenly, the power went out and we heard a loud noise outside. My son got a huge scare. I lit a candle and explained that it was only a tree that fell in the street.

paragraphs.pt: A luz voltou duas horas depois. Jantamos à luz de velas, conversamos e no fim achamos divertido. Fiquei aliviado porque ninguém se machucou.
paragraphs.en: The power came back two hours later. We had dinner by candlelight, talked and in the end found it fun. I was relieved because nobody got hurt.

questions.prompt: What was the narrator doing when the power went out?
O que fez barulho lá fora?
questions.explanation: The narrator explained it was only a tree that fell in the street.

questions.prompt: Why was the narrator relieved at the end?
questions.explanation: The last sentence says ninguém se machucou.

paragraphs.pt: Na tarde de ontem, uma ciclista de trinta e dois anos escapou de um acidente grave em Curitiba. Ela andava pela ciclovia, ouvindo música, quando um cachorro atravessou na frente da bicicleta.
paragraphs.en: Yesterday afternoon, a thirty-two-year-old cyclist escaped a serious accident in Curitiba. She was riding on the bike lane, listening to music, when a dog crossed in front of the bicycle.

paragraphs.pt: A ciclista freou, escorregou no chão molhado e caiu. Ela se machucou um pouco no joelho, mas não quebrou nenhum osso. Os bombeiros chegaram em dez minutos e levaram a mulher ao hospital por precaução.
paragraphs.en: The cyclist braked, slipped on the wet ground and fell. She hurt her knee a little, but did not break any bone. The firefighters arrived in ten minutes and took the woman to the hospital as a precaution.

paragraphs.pt: O dono do cachorro pediu desculpa e acompanhou a ciclista. Segundo ele, o animal se assustou com um barulho e saiu correndo. Felizmente, a mulher voltou pra casa no mesmo dia.
paragraphs.en: The dog's owner apologized and accompanied the cyclist. According to him, the animal got frightened by a noise and ran off. Luckily, the woman went home the same day.

questions.explanation: Ela andava pela ciclovia, ouvindo música.
She hurt her knee a little but did not break any bone.

exercises.prompt: Match the verb form with its meaning in a story

pairs.en: I met for the first time

exercises.explanation: A sudden event that moves the story forward uses the preterite.
